steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Memory is the process of encoding, storing and retrieving information. Encoding converts sensory input into a storable form; storage retains it; retrieval accesses it when needed. | Key Fact: The Multi-Store Model (Atkinson & Shiffrin, 1968): Sensory memory (brief, capacity limited by senses) -> Short-term memory (limited capacity 7+/-2 items, duration ~30 seconds) -> Long-term memory (potentially unlimited capacity and duration) via rehearsal. | Key Fact: Types of LTM: Episodic (personal experiences, e.g. your first day at school), Semantic (facts and knowledge, e.g. Paris is the capital of France), Procedural (skills and actions, e.g. riding a bike). | Key Fact: Eyewitness testimony is unreliable: Loftus & Palmer (1974) showed leading questions distort recall - participants est
